newsitem.title: UK: UN expects Iraq food plan by 2000 GMT Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: UN expects Iraq food plan by 2000 GMT Tuesday.

text.p: The United Nations hopes to receive the Iraqi food distribution plan by 2000 GMT on Tuesday, the U.N. coordinator in Baghdad said..
Staffan de Mistura told Reuters by telephone: "We expect to have a meeting at 7 o'clock (local time) which could last until midnight".
"My hope and expectation is that we will receive the Iraqi plan for the centre and south of the country (at that meeting)".
Iraqi time is four hours ahead of Greenwich Mean Time.
De Mistura said that U.N. agencies have had their distribution plan for the north ready for some time but were awaiting Iraq's plan for the centre and south of the country.
Iraq is permitted to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months, under U.N. supervision, to alleviate hardship caused by U.N. trade sanctions imposed on Baghdad for invading Kuwait in 1990.

The oil plan was first started in December last year and the U.N. Security Council renewed it for another 180 days on June 8. But the exports have been held up pending completion of the procurement and distribution plans by the government.

In the first six months Iraq earned about $1.3 billion, of which $260 million was earmarked for the northern provinces. De Mistura said Iraq would earn a similar amount of money in the next six months.
Iraq needs U.N. approval of both plans to be able to start selling oil on world markets again.
De Mistura said last week that about one million tonnes of food from the first partial sales had arrived in Iraq.
He said Iraq needed to resume sales again to keep humanitarian commodities arriving on a steady basis.
Oil markets have been watching developments in Baghdad keenly in recent days.
The price of oil has slumped nearly 30 percent this year, partly because of the resumption of Iraqi oil exports.
Seasonally weak summer demand has left the market vulnerable to a further downward move, said traders.
The International Energy Agency (IEA) said that oil prices are set to fall later this year as stocks rise despite higher than expected demand due to strong U.S. gasoline consumption this spring.

"The return of Iraqi crude to the export markets is the most important near-term wildcard for world oil supply. Over the last two weeks opinions regarding the likely date have varied widely ranging from mid-July to mid-August," the IEA said in latest Monthly Oil Market report.
"In recent days however more observers seem to be concluding that the return will be "later" rather than "sooner" but this could change.
